question: to the Commission Borja Giménez Larraz (PPE) Subject:

Decree-Law 3/2023 brought in authorisation arrangements putting an end to indefinite licences for short-term leases after five years. What is more, the granting of new licences is now subject to provisions of town-planning instruments, which municipalities such as Barcelona refuse to accept, thus placing a de facto obstacle in the way of the approval of such licences. This undermines the legal certainty of investments and raises a barrier to the internal market. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.

Whether it can it confirm that the authorities are restricting the internal market on the basis of sound scientific evidence demonstrating a causal link between short-term leases and housing shortages, or whether it supports the authorities’ discretion to restrict the free movement of services without any empirical justification?

Whether it believes these restrictions to be in compliance with the principles of ‘last resort’, proportionality, legal certainty and legitimate expectations, as well as with Articles 9, 10, 11 and 15 of the Services Directive?

Whether it considers that putting an end to existing licences after five years and making new licences contingent upon town-planning authorisations to be compatible with the freedom to provide services and EU case-law?
